category: Image Processing Toolbox > Import, Display, Geometry & Color
description: Reading and writing image files, displaying and comparing images, geometric transformations and registration, and conversions between image data types and colour spaces.

tools.name: imread
tools.description: Read an image from a graphics file into a MATLAB array. It supports dozens of formats (PNG, JPEG, TIFF, BMP, GIF, HDF, DICOM via dicomread) and infers the format from the file extension or contents. For indexed images it can also return the colormap and alpha channel.
tools.usage:
A = imread(filename)
A = imread(filename, fmt)
[A, map] = imread(___)
[A, map, alpha] = imread(___)
A = imread(filename, 'Index', k)

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: Path or URL of the image file.

parameters.name: fmt
parameters.description: Explicit format string such as 'png' or 'tif'.

parameters.name: 'Index'
parameters.description: Page/frame number for multipage TIFF or GIF files.

parameters.name: 'PixelRegion'
parameters.description: {[rows],[cols]} to read only a sub-rectangle of a large TIFF.

tools.notes: Data class depends on the file: usually uint8 or uint16. Convert with im2double before arithmetic.

tools.name: imwrite
tools.description: Write an array to a graphics file, choosing the format from the file extension or an explicit format argument. Format-specific name/value options control JPEG quality, PNG bit depth, TIFF compression and GIF animation. Use it to export results, figures or processed frames.
tools.usage:
imwrite(A, filename)
imwrite(A, map, filename)
imwrite(A, filename, fmt, Name, Value)

parameters.name: A
parameters.description: Image array (grayscale, RGB, or indexed with a map).

parameters.name: 'Quality'
parameters.description: JPEG quality 0-100 (default 75).

parameters.name: 'Compression'
parameters.description: TIFF compression: 'none', 'lzw', 'packbits', 'deflate'.

parameters.name: 'BitDepth'
parameters.description: Bits per pixel for PNG/JPEG output.

parameters.name: 'WriteMode'
parameters.description: 'overwrite' (default) or 'append' for multipage TIFF/GIF.

tools.name: imfinfo
tools.description: Return a structure array of metadata about an image file without reading the pixel data. Fields include width, height, bit depth, colour type, file size, and format-specific EXIF or TIFF tags. Use it to inspect large files cheaply or to branch on image properties before reading.
tools.usage:
info = imfinfo(filename)
info = imfinfo(filename, fmt)

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: Image file path or URL.

parameters.name: fmt
parameters.description: Explicit format if the extension is missing or wrong.

tools.example:
info = imfinfo('peppers.png');
fprintf('%dx%d, %s, %d bits\n', info.Width, info.Height, info.ColorType, info.BitDepth);

tools.name: imshow
tools.description: Display an image in a figure with the axes scaled so pixels are square and the image fills the available space. It handles grayscale, RGB, binary and indexed images, and the display range can be set explicitly or auto-scaled. This is the standard image display function.
tools.usage:
imshow(I)
imshow(I, [low high])
imshow(I, [])
imshow(X, map)
imshow(filename)
him = imshow(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: [low high]
parameters.description: Display range; [] auto-scales to the min and max of the data.

parameters.name: 'InitialMagnification'
parameters.description: 'fit' or a percentage.

parameters.name: 'Colormap'
parameters.description: Colormap to apply to a grayscale image.

parameters.name: 'Border'
parameters.description: 'tight' (default) or 'loose'.

tools.notes: For a double image imshow assumes the range [0 1]; pass [] to auto-scale instead of getting an all-white picture.

tools.name: imshowpair
tools.description: Display two images together to compare them, using a false-colour overlay, a difference image, or a side-by-side montage. It is the quickest way to check registration or the effect of a processing step. The 'falsecolor' method maps the two images to different colour channels so misalignment appears as colour fringes.
tools.usage:
imshowpair(A, B)
imshowpair(A, B, method)
imshowpair(A, RA, B, RB, method)
obj = imshowpair(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: method
parameters.description: 'falsecolor' (default), 'blend', 'diff', 'checkerboard' or 'montage'.

parameters.name: RA, RB
parameters.description: imref2d spatial referencing objects so images are shown in world coordinates.

parameters.name: 'Scaling'
parameters.description: 'independent' (default), 'joint' or 'none'.

tools.name: montage
tools.description: Display multiple images as a rectangular tiled montage in a single axes. It accepts a 4-D image stack, a cell array of images, an imageDatastore or a list of filenames. Use it to review a dataset, a set of filter outputs or the frames of a video at a glance.
tools.usage:
montage(I)
montage(filenames)
montage(imds)
montage(___, Name, Value)
img = montage(___)

parameters.name: 'Size'
parameters.description: [rows cols] tiling; use NaN for an automatically chosen dimension.

parameters.name: 'DisplayRange'
parameters.description: [low high] intensity range applied to all tiles.

parameters.name: 'BorderSize'
parameters.description: Padding between tiles in pixels.

parameters.name: 'ThumbnailSize'
parameters.description: [h w] to which each image is resized.

tools.example:
load mri
montage(D, map, 'Size', [4 7])
title('MRI slices')

tools.name: imtool
tools.description: Open the Image Viewer app, an interactive window with pixel inspection, zoom, pan, distance measurement, contrast adjustment and a pixel region tool. It is far more informative than imshow when you need to read individual pixel values or check local detail. Returns a handle so you can close it programmatically.
tools.usage:
imtool(I)
imtool(I, [low high])
imtool(filename)
htool = imtool(___)
imtool close all

parameters.name: I
parameters.description: Image array or filename.

parameters.name: [low high]
parameters.description: Display range; [] auto-scales.

parameters.name: 'InitialMagnification'
parameters.description: 'fit', 'adaptive', or a percentage.

tools.notes: Newer releases route imtool to the Image Viewer app. Requires a display.

tools.name: imresize
tools.description: Resize an image by a scale factor or to an explicit output size, with a choice of interpolation kernel. By default it applies an antialiasing lowpass filter when shrinking, which prevents moire artefacts. Use it for building image pyramids, normalizing dataset resolution and preparing network inputs.
tools.usage:
B = imresize(A, scale)
B = imresize(A, [numrows numcols])
B = imresize(A, ___, method)
[Y, newmap] = imresize(X, map, ___)

parameters.name: scale
parameters.description: Multiplicative scale factor, or [rows cols] with NaN to preserve aspect ratio.

parameters.name: method
parameters.description: 'nearest', 'bilinear', 'bicubic' (default), 'lanczos2', 'lanczos3'.

parameters.name: 'Antialiasing'
parameters.description: Logical; true by default when shrinking.

parameters.name: 'OutputSize'
parameters.description: Alternative name/value form of the target size.

tools.notes: Use 'nearest' for label/mask images so you do not invent intermediate label values.

tools.name: imrotate
tools.description: Rotate an image counterclockwise by a given angle in degrees, with a choice of interpolation and output sizing. The 'crop' option keeps the original frame size while 'loose' (default) grows the canvas to contain the whole rotated image. Use it for orientation correction and data augmentation.
tools.usage:
B = imrotate(A, angle)
B = imrotate(A, angle, method)
B = imrotate(A, angle, method, bbox)

parameters.name: angle
parameters.description: Rotation in degrees, counterclockwise for positive values.

parameters.name: method
parameters.description: 'nearest' (default), 'bilinear' or 'bicubic'.

parameters.name: bbox
parameters.description: 'loose' (default) to grow the output, or 'crop' to keep the input size.

tools.notes: Areas outside the original image are filled with zeros. For arbitrary transforms use imwarp.

tools.name: imcrop
tools.description: Crop an image to a rectangular region, either interactively by dragging on a displayed image or programmatically from a [xmin ymin width height] rectangle. It returns both the cropped image and the rectangle actually used. Use the programmatic form in scripts and the interactive form for exploration.
tools.usage:
Icropped = imcrop(I)
Icropped = imcrop(I, rect)
[Icropped, rect] = imcrop(___)
Icropped = imcrop(I, RI, rect)

parameters.name: rect
parameters.description: [xmin ymin width height] in pixel coordinates.

parameters.name: RI
parameters.description: imref2d object when the rectangle is in world coordinates.

tools.notes: The returned size is width+1 by height+1 because both endpoints are included. imcrop3 handles volumes.

tools.name: imtranslate
tools.description: Shift an image by a given number of pixels in x and y, with optional subpixel translation and interpolation. The FillValues option sets what appears in the vacated region, and OutputView controls whether the canvas grows. Use it for alignment tweaks and augmentation.
tools.usage:
B = imtranslate(A, translation)
B = imtranslate(A, translation, method)
[B, RB] = imtranslate(A, RA, translation, Name, Value)

parameters.name: translation
parameters.description: [tx ty] (or [tx ty tz] for volumes); non-integer values trigger interpolation.

parameters.name: method
parameters.description: 'linear' (default), 'nearest' or 'cubic'.

parameters.name: 'FillValues'
parameters.description: Value(s) used for pixels outside the original image.

parameters.name: 'OutputView'
parameters.description: 'same' (default) or 'full'.

tools.name: imwarp
tools.description: Apply a general geometric transformation object to an image or volume. It works with affine, projective, rigid, similarity, piecewise-linear and displacement-field transformations and returns the spatial referencing of the output. This is the engine behind imrotate, imtranslate and image registration.
tools.usage:
B = imwarp(A, tform)
[B, RB] = imwarp(A, RA, tform)
B = imwarp(A, D)
B = imwarp(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: tform
parameters.description: Geometric transformation object such as affinetform2d, rigidtform2d or projtform2d.

parameters.name: D
parameters.description: Displacement field for non-rigid warping.

parameters.name: 'OutputView'
parameters.description: imref2d specifying the output grid, e.g. to match a fixed image.

parameters.name: 'InterpolationMethod'
parameters.description: 'linear' (default), 'nearest' or 'cubic'.

parameters.name: 'FillValues'
parameters.description: Value for pixels mapped from outside the input.

tools.notes: In R2022b and later use the *tform2d objects (affinetform2d etc.) with premultiply convention; affine2d and projective2d are the older postmultiply equivalents.

tools.name: imref2d
tools.description: Create a spatial referencing object that ties image pixel indices to a world coordinate system with specified limits and pixel extents. Passing it to imshow, imwarp or imshowpair makes all operations happen in physical units such as millimetres. Essential when combining images of different resolutions or fields of view.
tools.usage:
R = imref2d()
R = imref2d(imageSize)
R = imref2d(imageSize, pixelExtentInWorldX, pixelExtentInWorldY)
R = imref2d(imageSize, xWorldLimits, yWorldLimits)

parameters.name: imageSize
parameters.description: Size vector [rows cols] of the referenced image.

parameters.name: pixelExtentInWorldX/Y
parameters.description: Physical size of one pixel in each direction.

parameters.name: xWorldLimits, yWorldLimits
parameters.description: Two-element world coordinate limits.

tools.notes: imref3d is the volumetric equivalent. Use worldToIntrinsic/intrinsicToWorld to convert coordinates.

tools.name: fitgeotform2d
tools.description: Estimate a 2-D geometric transformation from matched control point pairs. Supported types range from 'translation' and 'rigid' through 'similarity' and 'affine' to 'projective' and 'polynomial'. Use it in manual registration workflows and after feature matching.
tools.usage:
tform = fitgeotform2d(movingPoints, fixedPoints, transformationType)
tform = fitgeotform2d(movingPoints, fixedPoints, 'polynomial', degree)

parameters.name: movingPoints
parameters.description: n-by-2 [x y] coordinates in the image to be transformed.

parameters.name: fixedPoints
parameters.description: Matching n-by-2 coordinates in the reference image.

parameters.name: transformationType
parameters.description: 'translation', 'rigid', 'similarity', 'affine', 'projective', 'polynomial', 'pwl', 'lwm'.

tools.notes: Called fitgeotrans in releases before R2022b; that name still works but uses the older transformation classes.

tools.name: imregister
tools.description: Automatically align a moving image to a fixed image using intensity-based optimization. You choose 'monomodal' or 'multimodal' configuration and a transformation type, and it returns the registered image. It is the one-call entry point for intensity-based registration.
tools.usage:
movingReg = imregister(moving, fixed, transformType, optimizer, metric)
movingReg = imregister(moving, Rmoving, fixed, Rfixed, ___)
movingReg = imregister(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: transformType
parameters.description: 'translation', 'rigid', 'similarity' or 'affine'.

parameters.name: optimizer, metric
parameters.description: Objects returned by imregconfig.

parameters.name: 'PyramidLevels'
parameters.description: Number of multiresolution levels (default 3).

parameters.name: 'InitialTransformation'
parameters.description: Starting transform to seed the search.

tools.name: imregtform
tools.description: Estimate the geometric transformation that aligns a moving image to a fixed image, returning the transformation object instead of the warped image. This lets you inspect the transform, apply it to other images, or compose it with further transformations. Same optimizer/metric arguments as imregister.
tools.usage:
tform = imregtform(moving, fixed, transformType, optimizer, metric)
tform = imregtform(moving, Rmoving, fixed, Rfixed, ___)

parameters.name: transformType
parameters.description: 'translation', 'rigid', 'similarity' or 'affine'.

parameters.name: optimizer, metric
parameters.description: From imregconfig.

parameters.name: 'PyramidLevels'
parameters.description: Multiresolution level count.

tools.name: imregconfig
tools.description: Create a matched optimizer and similarity metric configuration for intensity-based registration. 'monomodal' uses a regular-step gradient descent with mean squares, suitable for images from the same sensor; 'multimodal' uses one-plus-one evolutionary optimization with Mattes mutual information for images from different modalities. Tune the returned objects' properties to improve convergence.
tools.usage: [optimizer, metric] = imregconfig(modality)

parameters.name: modality
parameters.description: 'monomodal' or 'multimodal'.

tools.name: imregdemons
tools.description: Perform non-rigid (deformable) registration using the diffeomorphic demons algorithm, returning a per-pixel displacement field. It handles local deformations that no global affine transform can capture, such as soft tissue motion. Apply the resulting field with imwarp.
tools.usage:
[D, movingReg] = imregdemons(moving, fixed)
[D, movingReg] = imregdemons(moving, fixed, N, Name, Value)

parameters.name: N
parameters.description: Iterations per pyramid level, e.g. [100 50 25].

parameters.name: 'AccumulatedFieldSmoothing'
parameters.description: Gaussian smoothing of the displacement field (default 1.0); larger is more regular.

parameters.name: 'PyramidLevels'
parameters.description: Number of multiresolution levels.

parameters.name: 'DisplayWaitbar'
parameters.description: Logical; set false in scripts.

tools.notes: Pre-align with imregister ('rigid' or 'affine') before running demons; it only handles small local deformations.

tools.name: im2gray
tools.description: Convert an RGB image to grayscale, passing a grayscale input through unchanged. This pass-through behaviour makes it safe to call in pipelines that may receive either colour or monochrome images, unlike rgb2gray which errors on 2-D input. Uses the same luminance weights as rgb2gray.
tools.usage: I = im2gray(RGB)

parameters.name: RGB
parameters.description: An m-by-n-by-3 colour image or an m-by-n grayscale image.

tools.name: rgb2gray
tools.description: Convert an RGB image or colormap to grayscale by forming a weighted sum 0.2989*R + 0.5870*G + 0.1140*B that matches human luminance perception. The output has the same class as the input. Use it as the first step of most classical image analysis pipelines.
tools.usage:
I = rgb2gray(RGB)
newmap = rgb2gray(map)

parameters.name: RGB
parameters.description: m-by-n-by-3 colour image of class uint8, uint16, single or double.

parameters.name: map
parameters.description: A colormap to convert to grayscale.

tools.notes: Errors if given a 2-D input; use im2gray in generic code.

tools.name: im2double
tools.description: Convert an image to class double, rescaling integer data into the range [0, 1]. This normalization is what most Image Processing Toolbox functions expect for floating-point images, so arithmetic does not saturate or wrap. Logical input becomes 0 and 1.
tools.usage:
J = im2double(I)
J = im2double(I, 'indexed')

parameters.name: I
parameters.description: Image of class uint8, uint16, int16, logical, single or double.

parameters.name: 'indexed'
parameters.description: Treat the input as an indexed image, adding 1 to integer indices.

tools.notes: double(I) merely changes class without rescaling; im2double also rescales. Use rescale for arbitrary range mapping.

tools.name: im2uint8
tools.description: Convert an image to class uint8, rescaling floating-point data from [0, 1] to [0, 255] and clipping values outside that range. Use it before writing results to common image file formats or to reduce memory usage. Values are rounded, so repeated conversions lose precision.
tools.usage:
J = im2uint8(I)
J = im2uint8(I, 'indexed')

parameters.name: I
parameters.description: Image of class double, single, logical, uint16 or int16.

parameters.name: 'indexed'
parameters.description: Treat the input as an indexed image.

tools.name: rgb2lab
tools.description: Convert RGB colour values to the CIE 1976 L*a*b* space, which is approximately perceptually uniform. Euclidean distance in L*a*b* corresponds much better to perceived colour difference than distance in RGB, which makes it the right space for colour segmentation and delta-E measurements. You can specify the colour space and white point.
tools.usage:
lab = rgb2lab(RGB)
lab = rgb2lab(RGB, Name, Value)

parameters.name: RGB
parameters.description: Image or n-by-3 list of RGB colour values.

parameters.name: 'ColorSpace'
parameters.description: 'srgb' (default), 'adobe-rgb-1998' or 'linear-rgb'.

parameters.name: 'WhitePoint'
parameters.description: 'd65' (default), 'd50', 'a', 'c', 'icc', or an XYZ triple.

tools.notes: lab2rgb performs the inverse. L* runs 0-100 while a* and b* are roughly -128 to 127.

tools.name: lab2rgb
tools.description: Convert CIE L*a*b* values back to RGB, with control over the target colour space, white point and output data type. Colours outside the RGB gamut are clipped. Use it after processing in L*a*b* to produce a displayable result.
tools.usage:
RGB = lab2rgb(lab)
RGB = lab2rgb(lab, Name, Value)

parameters.name: lab
parameters.description: L*a*b* image or n-by-3 colour list.

parameters.name: 'ColorSpace'
parameters.description: 'srgb' (default), 'adobe-rgb-1998' or 'linear-rgb'.

parameters.name: 'OutputType'
parameters.description: 'double', 'single', 'uint8' or 'uint16'.

tools.name: rgb2ycbcr
tools.description: Convert RGB to the YCbCr colour space used by JPEG, MPEG and most video standards, separating luminance (Y) from two chroma channels. Processing only the Y channel is a cheap way to enhance an image without shifting its colours. ycbcr2rgb performs the inverse.
tools.usage:
ycbcr = rgb2ycbcr(RGB)
ycbcrmap = rgb2ycbcr(map)

parameters.name: RGB
parameters.description: RGB image or colormap.

tools.notes: For uint8 data Y occupies 16-235 and Cb/Cr 16-240, following the ITU-R BT.601 studio range.

tools.name: imhist
tools.description: Compute and display the histogram of an image's intensity values. With output arguments it returns the bin counts and bin locations without plotting. Use it to judge exposure, choose thresholds and verify the effect of contrast adjustments.
tools.usage:
imhist(I)
imhist(I, n)
[counts, binLocations] = imhist(I)
imhist(X, map)

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Number of bins; defaults to 256 for uint8 and 2 for logical.

parameters.name: map
parameters.description: Colormap for indexed images.

tools.name: imadjust
tools.description: Map image intensity values from an input range to an output range, optionally with a gamma nonlinearity. Called with only the image it saturates the bottom and top 1% of pixels, which usually improves contrast immediately. Use it for simple, controllable contrast stretching.
tools.usage:
J = imadjust(I)
J = imadjust(I, [low_in high_in], [low_out high_out])
J = imadjust(I, ___, gamma)
J = imadjust(RGB, [lowRGB; highRGB], ___)

parameters.name: [low_in high_in]
parameters.description: Input range (0 to 1) to stretch; [] uses stretchlim defaults.

parameters.name: [low_out high_out]
parameters.description: Output range, default [0 1].

parameters.name: gamma
parameters.description: Curve shape; < 1 brightens, > 1 darkens, 1 (default) is linear.

tools.name: stretchlim
tools.description: Find the intensity limits that saturate a given fraction of pixels at the low and high ends of the histogram. Its output is designed to be passed straight to imadjust. Use it to make contrast stretching adaptive to each image rather than hard-coding limits.
tools.usage:
lowhigh = stretchlim(I)
lowhigh = stretchlim(I, tol)

parameters.name: tol
parameters.description: Scalar or [low high] fraction of pixels to saturate, default [0.01 0.99].

tools.name: histeq
tools.description: Enhance contrast by transforming intensities so the output histogram approximately matches a target distribution (flat by default). Global histogram equalization can dramatically reveal detail in low-contrast images but also amplifies noise and can look unnatural. For local control use adapthisteq.
tools.usage:
J = histeq(I)
J = histeq(I, n)
J = histeq(I, hgram)
[J, T] = histeq(___)

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Number of discrete output levels (default 64).

parameters.name: hgram
parameters.description: Target histogram to match instead of a uniform one.

parameters.name: T
parameters.description: Output transformation function that maps input to output levels.

tools.name: adapthisteq
tools.description: Contrast-Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE): equalize the histogram of many small tiles and interpolate between them, clipping the contrast enhancement to limit noise amplification. It brings out local detail across images with varying illumination, which global histeq cannot do. Widely used for medical and microscopy imagery.
tools.usage:
J = adapthisteq(I)
J = adapthisteq(I, Name, Value)

parameters.name: 'NumTiles'
parameters.description: [rows cols] tiling of the image, default [8 8].

parameters.name: 'ClipLimit'
parameters.description: 0 to 1 contrast limit (default 0.01); higher gives stronger enhancement.

parameters.name: 'Distribution'
parameters.description: 'uniform' (default), 'rayleigh' or 'exponential'.

parameters.name: 'NBins'
parameters.description: Histogram bins per tile (default 256).

tools.notes: For colour images apply it to the L channel of L*a*b* or the Y channel of YCbCr so hues do not shift.

tools.name: imhistmatch
tools.description: Adjust an image so its histogram matches that of a reference image. This is the standard way to normalize the appearance of images acquired under different lighting or by different scanners. Works on grayscale and colour images channel-wise.
tools.usage:
B = imhistmatch(A, ref)
B = imhistmatch(A, ref, N)
[B, hgram] = imhistmatch(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: A
parameters.description: Image to be adjusted.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: Reference image whose histogram is the target.

parameters.name: N
parameters.description: Number of histogram bins (default 64).

parameters.name: 'Method'
parameters.description: 'uniform' (default) or 'polynomial'.

tools.name: imcomplement
tools.description: Compute the photographic negative of an image: for integer types it subtracts each value from the maximum of the class, for double images from 1, and for logical it inverts. Useful when the objects of interest are dark on a light background and you want them bright for morphological processing. Many morphology operations assume bright foreground.
tools.usage: J = imcomplement(I)

parameters.name: I
parameters.description: Grayscale, binary, RGB or volumetric image.

tools.name: imlincomb
tools.description: Compute a linear combination of images, performing all arithmetic in double precision and rounding/saturating only once at the end. This avoids the intermediate truncation errors of chained imadd/imsubtract calls on integer images. Use it for blending, weighted averaging and unsharp masking.
tools.usage:
Z = imlincomb(K1, A1)
Z = imlincomb(K1, A1, K2, A2, ...)
Z = imlincomb(___, K)
Z = imlincomb(___, outputClass)

parameters.name: K1, K2, ...
parameters.description: Scalar weights.

parameters.name: A1, A2, ...
parameters.description: Images of the same size and class.

parameters.name: K
parameters.description: Optional scalar offset added at the end.

parameters.name: outputClass
parameters.description: Class of the result, e.g. 'uint8' or 'double'.

tools.name: imnoise
tools.description: Add synthetic noise of a specified type to an image: Gaussian, Poisson, salt & pepper, speckle or localvar. This is how you build test cases for denoising and robustness studies. The image is internally converted to double in [0, 1] before noise is applied.
tools.usage:
J = imnoise(I, 'gaussian', m, var)
J = imnoise(I, 'salt & pepper', d)
J = imnoise(I, 'speckle', var)
J = imnoise(I, 'poisson')
J = imnoise(I, 'localvar', V)

parameters.name: m, var
parameters.description: Mean and variance for Gaussian noise (defaults 0 and 0.01).

parameters.name: d
parameters.description: Noise density for salt & pepper (default 0.05).

parameters.name: V
parameters.description: Local variance image the same size as I.

tools.name: imfuse
tools.description: Create a single composite image from two images using false colour, blending, difference or checkerboard methods. Unlike imshowpair it returns the composite as an array rather than displaying it, so you can save or further process it. Useful for generating registration report figures.
tools.usage:
C = imfuse(A, B)
C = imfuse(A, B, method)
[C, RC] = imfuse(A, RA, B, RB, ___)
C = imfuse(___, 'ColorChannels', cc)

parameters.name: method
parameters.description: 'falsecolor' (default), 'blend', 'diff', 'montage', 'checkerboard'.

parameters.name: 'Scaling'
parameters.description: 'independent', 'joint' or 'none'.

parameters.name: 'ColorChannels'
parameters.description: [R G B] channel assignment such as [1 2 0] or 'red-cyan'.

tools.name: imtile
tools.description: Assemble a set of images into a single rectangular tiled image array. It is the programmatic counterpart to montage, returning an array rather than drawing a figure. Use it to build contact sheets that you can then save or feed into other functions.
tools.usage:
out = imtile(I)
out = imtile(filenames)
out = imtile(imds)
out = imtile(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: 'GridSize'
parameters.description: [rows cols], with NaN for an automatic dimension.

parameters.name: 'BorderSize'
parameters.description: Padding between tiles.

parameters.name: 'BackgroundColor'
parameters.description: Colour of the padding.

parameters.name: 'ThumbnailSize'
parameters.description: Size to which each image is resized.

tools.name: labeloverlay
tools.description: Overlay a label matrix or binary mask onto an image using coloured, semi-transparent regions. It is the standard way to visualize segmentation results on top of the original image. Colours and transparency are controllable, and a specific label can be suppressed as background.
tools.usage:
B = labeloverlay(A, L)
B = labeloverlay(A, BW)
B = labeloverlay(A, C)
B = labeloverlay(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: L / BW / C
parameters.description: Label matrix, binary mask, or categorical label image.

parameters.name: 'Colormap'
parameters.description: Colours for the labels, e.g. 'jet' or an n-by-3 matrix.

parameters.name: 'Transparency'
parameters.description: 0 (opaque) to 1 (invisible); default 0.5.

parameters.name: 'IncludedLabels'
parameters.description: Which label values to draw.

tools.name: imsplit
tools.description: Split a multichannel image into a separate array per channel in one call. It replaces the common pattern of indexing I(:,:,1), I(:,:,2) and I(:,:,3) individually. Works for any number of channels and returns a cell array when called with a single output.
tools.usage:
[C1, C2, C3] = imsplit(I)
C = imsplit(I)

parameters.name: I
parameters.description: m-by-n-by-c multichannel image.
